title: "Results"
subtitle: "Benchmark instances, solver runs, and reported metrics"
date: last-modified

This page summarizes solver results per model family. Tables are generated
from `experiments/**/summary.csv` files by
`scripts/generate_results_tables.py` — run that script and re-render the site
to refresh them (do not hand-edit content between the `AUTO-GENERATED`
markers below, it will be overwritten).

“Average steps” reports the mean number of spin flips per replica, averaged
across runs for an instance. The optional `average_steps` CSV column supplies
this value; “—” means step data was not recorded for every run. The leaderboard
shows the value from the selected result; steps do not affect its ranking.

To append solver output to a summary, run (from the repository root):

```bash
python example_notebook/Code/Modern/optimization/analizer.py \
  --input example_notebook/Code/Modern/optimization/results_greedy.txt \
  --program-name Greedy
python scripts/generate_results_tables.py
quarto render docs --to html
```

Use the matching input and program name for Random and Reluctant. The analyzer
appends rows, so rerunning it on the same file adds duplicates. It reads the
solver's first column as average steps, or the second column when PBS has
prepended a repeat counter, then averages the values by `(N, instance_seed)`.
Existing summaries are upgraded with the new column when needed; their older
rows retain blank step values.

Only the SK family is shown for now; other families are commented out below
(wrapped in `.content-hidden` divs) until there's real data for them.

# Leaderboard

Use the tabs to switch between system sizes. Within each table, one row is shown
per instance: the best run, ranked by lowest energy. Energies within an absolute
tolerance of 10⁻⁶ of the instance's lowest reported energy are treated as tied,
with ties broken by lowest TTS. This avoids ranking numerical differences below
the displayed precision ahead of runtime. Comparisons use the reported metrics;
the tolerance does not establish that two runs reached the same configuration.
